references.text: God promises Moses that He will teach him what to say. In [ref:Exod 4:12|Exodus 4:12], God assures Moses that He will put the words in His servant's mouth, which reflects Jesus' promise that disciples should not worry about what to say when brought before authorities.

God tells Jeremiah not to fear, for He will put His words in his mouth ([ref:Jer 1:7-9|Jeremiah 1:7-9]). This parallels the promise in Luke 12:11 that God will give disciples the words they need when required.

In [ref:Matt 10:17-20|Matthew 10:17-20], Jesus gives parallel teaching, warning disciples that they will be handed over to courts and synagogues, but the Father's Spirit will speak through them. This is a close parallel to Luke 12:11.

In [ref:Mark 13:11|Mark 13:11], Jesus says that when they are led away and handed over, they should not worry beforehand about what to say, for the Holy Spirit will speak through them. This is a direct parallel to Luke 12:11.

In [ref:Luke 21:12-15|Luke 21:12-15], Jesus repeats the promise in an eschatological context: disciples will be brought before synagogues and authorities, but He Himself will give them words and wisdom that no opponent can resist.

In [ref:Acts 4:8-12|Acts 4:8-12], we see the fulfillment of Jesus' promise, where Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, defends himself boldly before the Council without having prepared his speech—exactly as Jesus promised in Luke 12:11-12.

In [ref:Acts 6:10|Acts 6:10], Stephen's opponents could not withstand the wisdom and Spirit with which he spoke. This is a concrete fulfillment of the promise that the Holy Spirit will give disciples the right words.

In [ref:Acts 26:1-2|Acts 26:1-2], Paul defends himself before King Agrippa, an example of apostles being brought before authorities (ἀρχάς) and powers (ἐξουσίας), just as Jesus foretold in Luke 12:11.

Paul urges the Philippians not to be frightened by opponents ([ref:Phil 1:28|Philippians 1:28]). This boldness toward persecutors reflects the same attitude Jesus encourages in Luke 12:11—not to worry.
